chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The nahr (camel sacrifice) is in the labba (upper chest), and the dhabh (slaughter) is in the throat.'

key_terms.الذَّبْحُ: dhabh — the method of slaughter by cutting the throat, used for sheep, cattle, and most animals
key_terms.اللَّبَّةُ: labba — the upper chest or base of the neck; the site of camel slaughter
key_terms.النَّحْرُ: nahr — the method of slaughter for camels, involving stabbing at the base of the neck (labba)
key_terms.الْحَلْقُ: halq — the throat; the site of standard animal slaughter

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method of slaughtering a camel versus other animals in Islamic jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a key legal ruling in Islamic jurisprudence: the method of slaughter differs by animal type. The nahr — stabbing at the base of the neck (labba) — is the proper method for camels, while the dhabh — cutting the throat — is used for other animals such as cattle, sheep, and goats. This distinction is foundational in fiqh and is referenced in Quranic verses about sacrifice.
word_analysis: the nahr (camel sacrifice by stabbing the throat)
and the dhabh (slaughter by cutting the throat)
